q: Do TT bond ranks of single-exciton eigenstates of a periodic homogeneous NN chain actually grow (near-)linearly in N, or is there a finite plateau that r=15 already covers?
basis: Our sweep at ranks=15 saturates the middle bonds at 15 for N in {8,10,12}, so the observed rank profile [1,2,4,8,15,15,...,15,8,4,2,1] does not disprove the paper's claim but also does not confirm it. The paper reports 'often near-linear' but does not clearly separate 'intrinsic minimal rank' from 'chosen ALS ceiling'.
next_steps: Repeat the bench with ranks in {6,8,10,12,15,20,30,40} at each N in {6,8,10,12,14,16} and locate the accuracy elbow. Fit log(accuracy) vs r at each N; extract r_eff(N, tol=1e-6). Test the paper's claim as r_eff(N) = O(N^p) with a fitted p.

q: Why does N=8 max_err (1.9e-3) exceed both N=6 (1.0e-4) and N=10 (9.7e-15) despite identical ranks=15 and repeats=20?
basis: Our sweep shows non-monotone accuracy in N: N=4 machine precision, N=6 ~1e-4, N=8 ~2e-3, N=10 machine precision again. The 'good' N are exactly those where the chosen n_levels (N+1) fits inside the single-exciton band without needing to reach into the two-exciton subspace via deflation.
next_steps: Vary n_levels independently of N; compute overlap of ALS eigenvectors with two-exciton subspace projectors; test the hypothesis that accuracy drops precisely when deflation starts pushing the ALS iterate into a subspace with intrinsic TT rank > ranks. If confirmed, adaptive-rank ALS should erase the non-monotonicity.

q: Is the numpy same_kind casting failure in scikit_tt/solvers/evp.py a single latent bug or a symptom of a wider pattern where real operator init + complex deflation shift silently produced approximate (unchecked-precision) results on older NumPy?
basis: Two independent replications (this one and sibling PDE-Riedel-WaveTrain-tensor-trains-2023) converged on the same 4-line fix. Older NumPy (<1.20) would accept the cast silently by discarding the imaginary part of the deflation shift — potentially perturbing all excited-state ALS solutions computed by scikit_tt users prior to 2020 by an amount equal to the discarded imaginary shift term.
next_steps: Grep every python-quantum-chemistry / TT package on PyPI for the same anti-pattern (real-init tensor + complex outer-product deflation). Pin an old NumPy 1.18 env, run the same bench, and diff eigenstates against our modern-NumPy patched run to quantify how much accuracy was silently lost historically.

q: Do the paper's exciton-phonon coupled TDSE claims (Fig. 5-7) also require this evp.py patch, or does the SM-splitting time propagator avoid the deflation code path?
basis: We only exercised the TISE (eigenstate) path. The TDSE path uses Strang-Marchuk splitting, which does not call the ALS Wielandt deflation but does call scikit_tt.solvers.evp for the phonon-Hamiltonian ground state initialization in some driver scripts. If it hits the same code path, every TDSE simulation on modern NumPy is silently broken until patched.
next_steps: Run test_scripts/Exc_Pho_Coupling/tdse_1.py in the unpatched venv; if it crashes, verify identical fix works. Then run tdse_qe_*.py which use quasi-exact eigen init; those should not touch evp.py and should work unpatched.

q: How does WaveTrain's TT-ALS accuracy compare against a straight scipy.sparse.linalg.eigsh on the explicit Hamiltonian matrix at N=12 (dim 4096)?
basis: The paper motivates TT because full-Hilbert-space dim 2^N is intractable, but at N=12 the full matrix is only 4096x4096 = 16M complex entries = 256 MB — perfectly tractable on CherryRd. A direct scipy.sparse.linalg.eigsh on the assembled Hamiltonian would give an independent third reference (analytic tight-binding is already used; scipy would catch e.g. matrix-assembly bugs in WaveTrain that happen to be self-consistent). We did not attempt it.
next_steps: Assemble the N=12 Hamiltonian via wave_train's own hamilton.represent.matricize(), pass to scipy.sparse.linalg.eigsh(k=13, which='SM'), diff eigenvalues against our TT-ALS spectrum and against the analytic tight-binding. Automated regression check for future WaveTrain releases.
